texts: A persistent left superior vena cava with no innominate (bridging) vein must be cannulated when it floods the field and spoils drainage during bicaval bypass.
A left SVC drains into the coronary sinus, so with the caval tapes snugged its blood pours into the opened right atrium, distends the heart and reduces flow to the pump.
When a bridging innominate vein is present, the left SVC can be clamped because its blood can cross to the right; without one, clamping causes venous hypertension in the head and arm.
A sucker in the right atrium cannot keep up with the flow, and giving up the tricuspid repair is unnecessary.
In the picture, Franky pushes a third cannon into the second chimney on the left, which has no bridge to the first.
Memory hook: a second chimney with no bridge gets its own cannon.
